segments.text: Hey everyone, welcome back to the channel, today we're doing something super comforting.
quick shoutout to this video's sponsor, get twenty percent off your first order at the link below
okay so we're making garlic butter pasta, this is like my go-to when I don't want to think
reminds me of my mom's cooking honestly
alright let's get into it, first things first put a big pot of water on to boil, salt it generously
while that's coming up to temp, take about, let's say two hundred grams of spaghetti, we'll cook that later
now for the sauce, grab a pan, medium heat, and add a good glug of olive oil, just eyeball it
take four cloves of garlic, minced, and let that go in the oil until it's fragrant, maybe a minute or so
now add two tablespoons of butter — actually you know what, make it three, I like it really buttery
let the butter melt into the oil and garlic, swirl the pan a bit so it doesn't burn
oh also grab some red pepper flakes if you have them, totally optional but I love the heat
by now your water should be boiling, drop the spaghetti in and cook it according to the package, usually about nine minutes
make sure you save a cup of that starchy pasta water before you drain it, you'll need it in a sec
so funny story, one time I forgot to save the pasta water and the sauce just never came together right
anyway, once the pasta's about a minute from done, go ahead and drain it, reserving that water
toss the spaghetti straight into the garlic butter pan, add a splash of the pasta water, and toss it all together
the starch in that water is what makes the sauce cling to the noodles instead of just pooling at the bottom
now stir in the parmesan, get it nice and glossy, if it looks dry just add another splash of pasta water
season with salt and black pepper to taste, and finish with a handful of chopped parsley
by the way if your garlic ever starts turning brown too fast just pull the pan off the heat for a second
let it sit off heat for like thirty seconds before you plate, the sauce firms up a touch and clings better
plate it up, maybe a little extra parmesan and cracked pepper on top, and that's it, dinner in fifteen minutes
honestly this is basically the same base I use for my lemon garlic shrimp pasta too
anyway if you make this tag me, I love seeing your versions, and I'll see you in the next one
don't forget to like and subscribe, it really helps the channel out a ton
